title: AlphaTensor: Reinforcement Learning Discovers Faster Matrix Multiplication
whyItMatters: First AI system to surpass a 50-year human algorithmic record in core mathematics—finding a 47-multiplication 4×4 algorithm in mod 2 and 14,000+ novel factorizations.
summary: Published in Nature (Vol. 610), DeepMind's AlphaTensor framed matrix multiplication as a single-player 3D tensor-decomposition game played by an AlphaZero-style reinforcement learning agent. It improved the best-known scalar multiplication count for over 70 matrix sizes—including beating Volker Strassen's iconic 1969 49-multiplication 4×4 algorithm with 47 multiplications in finite-field arithmetic (ℤ₂)—while also optimizing hardware-specific GPU/TPU kernels.
technicalHighlights: Reduced 4×4 matrix multiplication in mod-2 arithmetic from Strassen's 49 multiplications (1969) to 47.
Discovered >14,000 non-equivalent rank-49 4×4 factorizations, revealing unexpected richness in algebraic complexity.
Pioneered the autonomous algorithm-discovery lineage culminating in FunSearch (2023) and AlphaEvolve (2025).
caveats: The 47-multiplication 4×4 breakthrough held in finite-field (characteristic 2) arithmetic rather than real/complex numbers—a gap later closed by AlphaEvolve's 48-multiplication complex algorithm in 2025.

scoreRationale.foundational: Proved deep RL can autonomously discover mathematically novel, provably exact fundamental algorithms beyond human intuition.
scoreRationale.ripple: Launched the AI-for-algorithm-discovery subfield directly leading to AlphaDev, FunSearch, and AlphaEvolve.
scoreRationale.verification: Every tensor factorization is algebraically exact, published in Nature, and openly released for deterministic checking.
scoreRationale.velocity: Broke a 53-year algorithmic standstill and accelerated automated search across discrete math.
